To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

geometrically-tuned suture interfaces can achieve an order of magnitude increase in stiffness and toughness over conventional suture interfaces, and that this can be achieved with a wide range of deformation and failure behaviors, including brittle and ductile, and with or without a bonded tip region.
the mechanical properties of suture interfaces are tunable by the presence or absence and geometry of a bonded tip, the tip angle and the geometry.
geometric parameters of the suture interface, including the bonded tip, tip angle, tooth geometry, and tooth size, govern the mechanical behavior of suture interfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and characterization of bioinspired suture interfaces, which are of importance to the field of soft robotics and other applications.
the mechanics of geometrically structured suture interfaces in biological and synthetic systems.
understanding the mechanical behavior of bio-inspired, 3D printed, geometrically structured suture interfaces and the role of geometry in governing their mechanical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geometric parameters (tip bonding, tip angle and geometry), in addition to the material properties, can be utilized to design suture interfaces with tunable and amplified properties.
suture interface designs with a bonded tip, trapezoidal geometry, and large tip angle promote the greatest amplifications of mechanical properties.

the geometric parameters of the interface (bonded tip region, tip angle, tip geometry) and the geometry of the interface (rectangular, trapezoidal, triangular, anti-trapezdoidal) can be tuned to produce suture interfaces with tailored stiffness, strength, toughness, failure mechanism, and failure behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tip bonding and tip geometry are important for suture interfaces, which are the most common type of interface in the human body.
we have developed a new class of suture interfaces that are capable of achieving a wide range of properties by varying the geometric parameters, including a new type of interface with a bonded tip.
we have demonstrated a design space that allows for a wide range of mechanical behavior in suture interfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geometry of the suture interface, in particular the tip geometry, can be used to tune the mechanical properties of the suture.
the geometry and bonding of suture interfaces can be used to tailor the mechanical behavior of the interface.
the design of suture interfaces with tailored mechanical properties is possible by tuning the tip bonding, tip angles, and geometry of the suture interface.
